LESSON: GOOD CITIZENSHIP IN SCHOOL

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Citizenship and Governance in Kenya
Topic 5.1: Good citizenship in school
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Good citizenship in school, part of Citizenship and Governance in Kenya in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we demonstrate good citizenship in school? 2. Why is good citizenship in school important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Good citizenship in school together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: learners network as they undertake group activities and exchange new ideas as they design a poster

with qualities of a good citizen in school

● Citizenship: learners develop information and communication skills as they engage a resource person to discuss the importance

of good citizenship

Values:
● Social justice: learners cooperate as they use digital or print resources to identify qualities of a good citizen in school

● Peace: learners exhibit care as they respect self and others as they brainstorm in groups qualities of a good citizen in school

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs) :

● Honesty: learners speak, sign and act honestly as they discuss in groups how to become a good citizen in school

● Social cohesion: learners develop harmonious coexistence as they discuss in groups how to become a good citizen in school

Links to other Learning Areas:
English and Kenya Sign Language: as learners write an essay on a good digital citizen (using technology positively) and share the essays

in class.
